verified.exploit_entry_point: MCP tool execute_sql with a read-only tool configuration; the tool calls the connector's public executeSQL contract, and the security suites drive both the real handler and that contract against in-process engine stand-ins that follow the database rules (read-only transactions, SQLite query_only, MySQL comment lexing, SQL Server transactional rollback).
sites: src/connectors/postgres/index.ts:598-666 (single and batch paths ignore ExecuteOptions.readonly)
src/connectors/mariadb/index.ts:593-643 (same gap in a separate connector)
src/connectors/sqlite/index.ts:451-565 (shared handle; no per-call engine guard)
src/utils/allowed-keywords.ts:89-122 (every pragma form admitted as read-only)
routes: T1: a function call, a data-selecting CTE, and a later batch statement through a read-only PostgreSQL tool
T2: the same on a MariaDB source through the separate connector
T4: a direct INSERT and a batch that turns the engine guard off first, handed to a read-only SQLite execution
T6: assignment, tight-assignment, parenthesized, application_id, and query_only setter pragma forms through the read-only SQLite tool
T9: a DROP and an INSERT hidden after --x through the read-only MariaDB tool
T5: INSERT, batch UPDATE and DELETE handed to a read-only SQL Server execution
coupled: ordinary read-only queries on every source, writable tools on the same sources, SQLite introspection pragmas, and the existing comment/function-call handling
verified.project_tests_run: The project's own vitest unit tests for the affected area (allowed-keywords, sql-parser, execute-sql) plus 6 hidden functional files: 211 functional tests, on the pinned tree, the reference fix and every check patch; 19 hidden security tests.
verified.local_runs: pinned: security 0/19, functional 211/211; oracle: 19/19 and 211/211; each miss patch: its own concept's security tests fail with functional 211/211; upstream_fix: SQL Server security tests fail, functional 211/211; wrong-fix and alternative patches behaved as declared.

traps.shape: the per-request read-only option is declared on the connector contract and passed on every execution, but the PostgreSQL connector never reads it, on either the single-statement or the batch path, so a write hidden in an allow-listed statement (a function call, a data-selecting CTE, a later batch statement) executes
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the connector contract calls this application-level keyword validation already performed at the tool gate, and the product docs call read-only mode a safety net rather than a security boundary, so the connector reads as the wrong layer
traps.realistic_because: published advisory route (GHSA-mwwr-p57h-56pf) at the pinned commit

traps.shape: the MariaDB connector is a separate implementation of the same contract and does not share code with the MySQL connector, so a fix made in one does not reach the other
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the MariaDB connector mirrors the MySQL one line for line and both are registered implementations of the same interface, so a fix in the MySQL connector is assumed to cover it
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code the published fix touches

traps.shape: SQLite keeps one process-local handle opened at connect and the per-request read-only option is ignored, so a write that reaches the connector executes on the shared handle; a connection-level read-only open is impossible for an in-memory database
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the handle is opened once and an in-memory database cannot be opened read-only, so read-only can only be a decision made above the connector
traps.realistic_because: published advisory route (the consolidated SQLite engine gap) at the pinned commit

traps.shape: every pragma form is admitted as read-only, including the assignment and parenthesized setter forms, while rejecting pragmas wholesale would break the introspection forms the project's own tests require
traps.reason_to_dismiss: pragma is the SQLite introspection keyword and the pinned unit test requires PRAGMA table_info(users) to be read-only, so rejecting pragmas or their parenthesized form looks like it would break legitimate schema discovery
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code (the advisory's SQLite pragma gap)

traps.shape: two dashes are always treated as a comment, while MySQL and MariaDB only begin one after whitespace, a control character or end of line, so a statement written after --x is hidden from the admission decision and executed
traps.reason_to_dismiss: two dashes begin a comment in SQL, so the whitespace/control-character nuance reads as an obscure lexical detail that the execution-layer backstop will cover anyway
traps.realistic_because: published advisory route (GHSA-j656-3hf2-fvjc) at the pinned commit

traps.shape: the SQL Server connector has no read-only enforcement at all, and the published fix does not touch it; a write handed to a read-only execution reaches the server
traps.reason_to_dismiss: T-SQL has no READ ONLY transaction, the driver is optional, and the published remediation is scoped to the dialects it patched, so there is nothing obvious to do
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code the published fix never touched
